# README

# repo-aeo — Repo Discoverability Kit (RDK)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![Node >= 18](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D18-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org)

Make any repository, npm package and docs site **findable and recommendable** for
humans, AI agents and search engines.

RDK scores how discoverable your repository is, fixes the parts that can be fixed
automatically, and keeps it from regressing in CI. It is the tool you point at a
repo that is *good but invisible*.

The audit runs **41 checks in under 200 ms offline** on this repository
(measured with `rdk audit --format json`, `duration_ms` field) and carries **0
runtime dependencies**, so `npx` stays fast and the supply chain stays small.

## Quickstart

**Prerequisites:** Node.js >= 18

```bash
# 1. add RDK to your repository
npm install --save-dev @repo-aeo/rdk-cli

# 2. scaffold the config and the missing files
npx rdk init --apply

# 3. see the score and the prioritised fix list
npx rdk audit

# 4. run the test suite
npm test
```

Two-minute setup for a repository you do not own yet: clone it, run
`npx rdk init --apply`, then `npx rdk audit`. Everything the CLI writes is a
reviewable diff — it never publishes, tags or force-pushes. The one exception
lives in CI: the opt-in autofix job force-pushes its own dated
`rdk/autofix-<date>` bot branch and opens a reviewable PR.

## Who is it for

- Maintainers publishing an npm package for the first time.
- Teams whose library is good but invisible in AI answers, npm search and GitHub search.
- Agent-tooling authors who want their repo to be usable by coding agents out of the box.
- Researchers and OSS projects that need citation and discovery metadata.

## What you get

Three layers, because a one-off script is not enough:

| Layer | What it is | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Repo Kit** | `.discoverability/project.yml` as the single source of truth, plus templates and generators | `.discoverability/`, `packages/rdk-cli/src/generate/` |
| **Skillpack** | Agent instructions with progressive disclosure: audit → plan → patch → verify | `skills/repo-discoverability/` |
| **Automation** | GitHub Action on `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch` and weekly cron | `.github/workflows/rdk-audit.yml`, `action/action.yml` |
| **Monitoring** | MCP server with 8 read-mostly tools, trend history and live GitHub / site / npms probes | `packages/repo-aeo-mcp/` |

## Commands

```bash
npx rdk init          # create .discoverability/project.yml + minimal safe files
npx rdk audit         # score 0-100 + findings (json | markdown | github-comment)
npx rdk fix           # preview safe autofixes; --apply to write them
npx rdk npm-surface   # package.json publish surface + npm pack --dry-run
npx rdk github-sync   # push description/homepage/topics (needs --apply --ack --reason)

npx repo-aeo-mcp serve # the same engine as an MCP server: 8 read-mostly tools
claude mcp add rdk -- npx repo-aeo-mcp serve
docker run -i repo-aeo-mcp serve
```

Every write operation requires an explicit flag. `audit` is read-only and works
offline; `--online` adds link checks and live GitHub metadata.

## Examples

### 1. Score a repository

```bash
$ npx rdk audit            # measured on fixtures/demo-repo, offline
score: 29/100 (grade F) · checks: 10/41 passed · findings: 12 error, 13 warn, 6 info (16 autofixable) · mode: offline (use --online for link + GitHub checks)
```

### 2. Fix what is safe to fix

```bash
$ npx rdk fix --dry-run     # review the diff
$ npx rdk fix --apply       # 18 files: README sections, AGENTS.md draft, llms.txt, CITATION.cff, ...
```

### 3. Check the publish surface

```bash
$ npx rdk npm-surface --pack
| exports | conditions: import, require; subpaths: . |
⚠️ present in the repo but not in the tarball: llms.txt
```

### 4. Keep it from regressing in CI

```yaml
# .github/workflows/rdk-audit.yml (already in this repo)
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with: { node-version: '22' }
- run: npx --yes @repo-aeo/rdk-cli@^0.1.0 audit --format github-comment --online
- run: npx --yes @repo-aeo/rdk-cli@^0.1.0 audit --format json --online --min-score "${{ github.event.inputs.min_score || vars.RDK_MIN_SCORE || 0 }}"
```

The CLI itself never force-pushes; the workflow's opt-in autofix job (gated by
`safety.allow_autofix`) force-pushes only its own dated `rdk/autofix-<date>`
bot branch and opens a PR for review.

### 5. Monitor it continuously

```bash
$ npx repo-aeo-mcp score
Discoverability score: 96/100 (grade A)
checks passed: 39/41 - errors 0 - warnings 0 - autofixable 0
trend: no history yet
```

The first run records the score; every subsequent run prints the delta instead
(for example `trend: 90 -> 96 (up)`).

### 6. Teach an agent to do it

```text
skills/repo-discoverability/SKILL.md → description triggers on
"make repo discoverable", "add topics", "improve README for users and agents",
"prepare npm metadata", "generate AGENTS.md", "optimize for AI search"
```

## Use cases

- Score a repository's discoverability and get a prioritised fix list.
- Generate and maintain `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for a repo.
- Prepare `package.json` metadata, exports and tarball contents before an npm release.
- Fill GitHub description, homepage and 8–20 topics from one config file.
- Keep discoverability from regressing with a weekly GitHub Action audit.
- Watch score, npm search score and GitHub signals from an MCP client or a cron job.

## Discoverability Score

Six weighted axes, renormalised over the axes that apply to your project:

| Axis | Weight | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub metadata | 20 | description, homepage, 8–20 topics |
| README primitives | 25 | first success path, 2–5 examples, audience sections, sourced claims |
| Agent readiness | 15 | `AGENTS.md` with working commands, do/don't rules |
| npm readiness | 20 | description, keywords, exports, types, tarball hygiene |
| Docs readiness | 12 | `llms.txt`, JSON-LD, link health |
| Trust & hygiene | 8 | LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODEOWNERS, no leaked secrets |

Grades: A ≥ 90 · B ≥ 80 · C ≥ 70 · D ≥ 55 · F below. Full model:
[`docs/scoring.md`](./docs/scoring.md).

## Why choose this

- **One config file drives everything.** `.discoverability/project.yml` feeds the
  README, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, npm metadata and GitHub topics — no drift
  between them.
- **Same audit locally and in CI.** Ships as a CLI, an agent skill and a GitHub
  Action, so a human and an agent run identical checks.
- **Audit-only by default.** Writes need an explicit flag; publish/tag/release
  are out of scope entirely and require a human ACK string.
- **Deterministic generators.** Zero runtime dependencies, no LLM in the loop:
  every generated line is traceable to the config or to a file in the repo.

## How RDK compares

Most tools in this space anchor to a **served website** (llms.txt validators,
GEO graders, Lighthouse), a **published package** (npms.io) or a **docs build**
(framework generators). RDK anchors to the **git working tree**: it audits and
repairs the repository itself, before anything is served or published.

### Direct comparables: repo-local artifact graders and generators

| Tool | Unit of analysis | Scores | Generates | Validates | Writes to GitHub | Agent interface | CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **RDK (this repo)** | git working tree | 0-100 rubric, 6 axes | llms.txt, llms-full.txt, AGENTS.md, JSON-LD, CITATION.cff, templates | freshness, structure, link probes (`--online`) | guarded sync (ack + reason + preview) | MCP server + agent skill | composite Action |
| [repo-health-radar](https://github.com/xxrraa/repo-health-radar) | git working tree | 0-100 + letter grade, 6 human-maintainer axes | - | 35 checks (docs, CI, release readiness, activity) | - | - | composite Action |
| [GitHub community profile](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/about-community-profiles-for-public-repositories) | repo, hosted checklist | checklist | - | presence + supported location of trust files | - | - | built into github.com |
| [standard-readme](https://github.com/RichardLitt/standard-readme) + [remark preset](https://github.com/RichardLitt/standard-readme-preset) | README.md | pass/fail lint | scaffold only | section spec for human readers | - | - | remark CLI |
| [readme-score](https://github.com/clayallsopp/readme-score), [ReadmeAI](https://github.com/eli64s/readme-ai), README templates | README.md | richness proxies (code blocks, images) | LLM-written README | - | - | - | - |
| [cffinit](https://github.com/citation-file-format/cff-initializer-javascript) / [cffconvert](https://github.com/citation-file-format/cffconvert) | CITATION.cff | - | CFF via a human form / format conversions | version-pinned JSON schemas | - | - | [reject-only gate](https://github.com/citation-file-format/cffconvert-github-action) |
| [codemeta-generator](https://github.com/codemeta/codemeta-generator) | a GitHub repo page | - | CodeMeta JSON-LD | JSON-LD context | - | - | - |
| [npms.io](https://npms.io/about) | published package | quality/maintenance/popularity | - | - | - | - | - |
| [Repomix](https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix) / [ai-digest](https://github.com/khromov/ai-digest) | repo content | - | one packed context file | secret scan before output | - | CLI/MCP consumption | - |

### Adjacent territory: sites, indexes and agent context

| Tool | Unit of analysis | Scores | Generates | Validates | Writes to GitHub | Agent interface | CI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Lighthouse Agentic Browsing](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/agentic-browsing/llms-txt) | served site | pass/fail audits | - | llms.txt presence, H1, links | - | - | via Lighthouse CI |
| [llms-txt-hub](https://github.com/thedaviddias/llms-txt-hub) / [llms-txt-check](https://github.com/portdeveloper/llms-txt-check) | served site | - | - | presence at visit time; file claims vs what the site serves | - | browser extension | - |
| Framework generators ([Starlight](https://github.com/delucis/starlight-llms-txt), [mkdocs](https://github.com/pawamoy/mkdocs-llmstxt), Docusaurus, Mintlify) / [firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/llmstxt-generator) | docs build or crawl | - | llms.txt (+ full) at build time | - | - | - | docs pipeline |
| [agentmarkup](https://github.com/agentmarkup/agentmarkup) | site build | - | llms.txt, JSON-LD, markdown mirrors | yes, at build | - | - | build step |
| [geo-score](https://github.com/jianruntech/geo-score) and GEO skill packs / [Searchstack](https://github.com/alexpospekhov/searchstack-aeo) | served site / external AI engines | 0-100 rubric | - | crawlability, markup, citations; brand visibility in AI answers | - | skill pack | cron |
| [DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com) and [open-source](https://github.com/AsyncFuncAI/deepwiki-open) [clones](https://github.com/AIDotNet/OpenDeepWiki) | public repo, hosted | - | auto-wiki and diagrams | - | - | remote MCP | - |
| [Context7](https://github.com/upstash/context7) / [mcpdoc](https://github.com/langchain-ai/mcpdoc) | third-party docs | - | - | - | - | MCP consumption of llms.txt | - |
| [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard), Socket, Snyk | repo / dependencies, security | 0-10 risk-weighted aggregate | - | supply-chain risk | results only | Socket MCP | scorecard-action |
| [CHAOSS](https://github.com/chaoss/metrics) / [libraries.io](https://github.com/librariesio/libraries.io) | community events / package index | metric catalog, no composite | dashboards | - | - | - | self-hosted platform |

Orthogonal by design: Scorecard grades how safe a repo is to consume,
community standards grade human onboarding, packers serialize content,
DeepWiki hosts a generated wiki and CHAOSS measures community behaviour over
time. None of them repairs the repository; RDK does not replace any of them.

### Where RDK is deliberately narrower

- **No codebase packing.** Repomix and ai-digest ship the repo as one context
  file; RDK points agents at the right files (llms.txt, AGENTS.md) instead of
  serializing content.
- **No CFF schema validation.** RDK generates a CITATION.cff stub; validating
  it against the versioned schema is cffconvert's job, and the community's
  fix story there is reject-in-CI, never rewrite.
- **One root llms.txt pair.** No per-path or per-section corpora like Ray's
  sectioned `llms-full.txt` files or Cloudflare's per-product variants.
- **Repo-local llms.txt checks.** "Does the served site match the file" is
  only an MCP tool and an `--online` probe, not a full served-vs-file diff
  like llms-txt-check.
- **npms.io is fetched, not computed.** If npms.io goes away, the npm axis
  falls back to registry metadata only.
- **The ack string is a reusable constant.** A determined model can type it;
  single-use, argument-bound tokens (as in mature write-gated MCP servers)
  close that loop tighter. Preview-by-default and the reason audit log are
  the compensating controls here.
- **The rubric is heuristic, not observational.** A 96/100 means the repo
  satisfies the checks, not that it outranks anything in a population-wide
  model like npms.io's.
- **No activity or adoption axis.** repo-health-radar and CHAOSS grade
  maintainer responsiveness, release cadence and contributor diversity from
  event history; RDK scores artifacts only, so a well-documented dead repo
  scores high here.
- **No visibility-in-engines measurement.** Searchstack probes Google, AI
  Overviews and chat assistants about your brand; RDK can only make the repo
  legible, never observe how engines actually rank it.
- **Location-awareness of trust files is GitHub's job.** The community
  profile accepts CODE_OF_CONDUCT in `.github/`, root or `docs/`; RDK's checks
  look at fixed paths.

### Where RDK leads

- The only tool above whose unit of analysis is the working tree: everything
  is fixable before the first deploy or publish. The nearest twin,
  repo-health-radar, shares the shape (zero-dep CLI, composite action,
  min-score gate) but grades human-maintainer axes and ships no autofixes,
  MCP server or agent artifacts.
- README primitives are scored for agent consumption (install-command
  detectability, quickstart placement, parseable structure); the numeric
  README graders that exist reward human presentation instead.
- Cross-source coherence (config vs package.json vs GitHub vs README) has no
  analog; topic managers are write-only wrappers.
- Double-run idempotency (`rdk fix` twice produces no diff) is a tested gate,
  where codemod ecosystems treat it as folklore.
- A write-guarded MCP tool with reason logging and tool annotations on every
  tool, in a zero-runtime-dependency package that audits fully offline.

## Status

Actively developed. v0.1 ships the CLI, the skill, the Action **and** the MCP
server. IDE packaging is next
([roadmap issues](https://github.com/WhiteBite/repo-aeo/issues)).

## Repository map

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/rdk-cli/` | the `@repo-aeo/rdk-cli` package (zero dependencies) |
| `packages/repo-aeo-mcp/` | the `repo-aeo-mcp` MCP server (8 tools, stdio, Dockerfile) |
| `skills/repo-discoverability/` | SKILL.md + references + scripts for coding agents |
| `action/`, `.github/workflows/` | GitHub Action and reusable composite action |
| `fixtures/demo-repo/` | before/after demo repository |
| `docs/` | architecture, configuration, scoring, MCP plan, links |
| `REPORT.md` | real audit output and PR comment sample |
